title: Tavot Rishba

paragraphs: Shmuel’s student: [Shabbat 17b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.17b.1) and [Shabbat 146b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.146b.8) have Tavot (or Tavi) Rishba speaking in Shmuel’s name. In [Taanit 10a](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.10a.13), they ask Shmuel when to begin requesting dew and rain. He answers: “When firewood is brought into Tavot Rishba’s house.” [Rashi on Shabbat 17b](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Shabbat.17b.1.2) explains that he spread nets to hunt animals and birds. The Arukh, under rishba, cites a Gaon’s interpretation that he was the head of a family division, the initials resh bet av forming rishba. [Midrash Shmuel 25:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Shmuel.25.3) has Tavot speaking in Shmuel’s name; perhaps he is Tavot Rishba.[^3]

notes.text: ציבי means firewood here, not gazelle-hunters. The questioners are unnamed; the earlier draft’s Rav Yehudah was unsupported. Rashi’s hunter explanation and the Arukh’s head-of-family interpretation remain distinct.

The Taanit 10a firewood account was directly inspected. The distinct Rashi, Arukh and Midrash Shmuel explanations are retained as Hyman reports them; they do not independently establish that every Tavot is the same person.

Shabbat 17b calls the transmitter Tavi, and Shabbat 146b and Taanit call him Tavot. Midrash Shmuel gives Tavot without Rishba. The two explanations of Rishba and Hyman’s tentative identification remain distinct.
